lessons.title: What Is Frontend Development?
lessons.description: Understand what frontend engineers actually build, how frontend differs from design and backend work, and why HTML, CSS, and JavaScript are the starting point.

lessons.title: How the Web Works
lessons.description: Build the core mental model of the web: a browser sends a request to a server, the server sends back a response, and the browser uses that response to continue building the experience.

lessons.title: What Happens When You Click a Link?
lessons.description: Follow a webpage request from a user's click through DNS, the server response, and the browser's first rendering steps.
lessons.topicTitle: What Happens When You Click A Link

lessons.title: Browser, Server, and Client
lessons.description: Understand the different jobs of the browser and server, why the browser is called the client, and which responsibilities belong on each side of a web application.

lessons.title: How Forge Works
lessons.description: Learn how Forge's Learn, Practice, and Grow loop turns lessons into active skill-building, and understand what to do after you finish a lesson.

lessons.title: HTML: The Structure of the Web
lessons.description: Write your first HTML, understand what elements and nesting are, and build a tiny page using meaningful structure instead of visual guesswork.
lessons.levelTitle: Level 1: Core Web Standards & Styling Architecture
lessons.topicTitle: Html The Structure Of The Web

lessons.title: Elements, Tags, and Attributes
lessons.description: Learn how HTML elements are written, how opening and closing tags create structure, and how attributes provide additional information.
lessons.levelTitle: Level 1: Core Web Standards & Styling Architecture

lessons.title: Headings, Paragraphs, and Text
lessons.description: Practice using HTML headings and paragraphs to create a clear document structure that communicates hierarchy to both people and the browser.
lessons.levelTitle: Level 1: Core Web Standards & Styling Architecture

lessons.title: Links, Images, and Paths
lessons.description: Practice using anchors and images correctly, understand how href and src point to resources, and learn how relative and absolute paths are resolved by the browser.
lessons.levelTitle: Level 1: Core Web Standards & Styling Architecture

lessons.title: Lists and Tables
lessons.description: Practice using HTML lists to represent ordered or unordered collections and tables to represent genuine tabular data.
lessons.levelTitle: Level 1: Core Web Standards & Styling Architecture

lessons.title: Forms and User Input
lessons.description: Build forms that collect user input using labels, inputs, and a submit action, and learn why associating labels with controls is essential for usable HTML.
lessons.levelTitle: Level 1: Core Web Standards & Styling Architecture

lessons.title: Semantic HTML
lessons.description: Learn how semantic HTML elements communicate the role of page regions and content, then refactor generic markup into meaningful structure that is easier to navigate, maintain, and understand.
lessons.levelTitle: Level 1: Core Web Standards & Styling Architecture

lessons.title: HTML Challenge: Build a Real Page
lessons.description: Bring the HTML module together by building a complete page that uses headings, text, links, images, lists, forms, and semantic structure in one coherent document.
lessons.levelTitle: Level 1: Core Web Standards & Styling Architecture
lessons.topicTitle: Html Challenge Build A Real Page

lessons.title: What Is CSS?
lessons.description: Understand CSS as a rule-based styling language, learn the anatomy of a CSS rule, and build the mental model that styles are matched to elements and then resolved.
lessons.levelTitle: Level 1: Core Web Standards & Styling Architecture

lessons.title: Selectors and Specificity
lessons.description: Learn how CSS identifies elements with type, class, ID, attribute, and descendant selectors, then understand why conflicting rules do not all have equal priority.
lessons.levelTitle: Level 1: Core Web Standards & Styling Architecture

lessons.title: The Cascade and Inheritance
lessons.description: Understand how the CSS cascade resolves competing declarations, how inherited properties flow from parent to child, and why !important should not be your first response to a styling conflict.
lessons.levelTitle: Level 1: Core Web Standards & Styling Architecture

lessons.title: The CSS Box Model
lessons.description: Understand how every HTML element becomes a box made of content, padding, border, and margin, and learn how the browser calculates the space that element occupies.
lessons.levelTitle: Level 1: Core Web Standards & Styling Architecture

lessons.title: Spacing, Sizing, and Layout
lessons.description: Turn the box model into practical layout skills by controlling width, height, spacing, and gaps while learning to distinguish element size from the space around it.
lessons.levelTitle: Level 1: Core Web Standards & Styling Architecture

lessons.title: Typography and Text
lessons.description: Learn how CSS controls typography, including font family, size, weight, line height, alignment, and readable text width.
lessons.levelTitle: Level 1: Core Web Standards & Styling Architecture

lessons.title: Colors, Backgrounds, and Borders
lessons.description: Learn how CSS controls foreground and background colors, borders, rounded corners, and simple visual surfaces while keeping contrast and content accessibility in mind.
lessons.levelTitle: Level 1: Core Web Standards & Styling Architecture

lessons.title: Display and Normal Flow
lessons.description: Understand how block and inline elements participate in normal document flow, how the display property changes that behavior, and why layout bugs often begin with misunderstanding the flow.
lessons.levelTitle: Level 1: Core Web Standards & Styling Architecture

lessons.title: Flexbox Fundamentals
lessons.description: Learn how Flexbox arranges elements along a main axis and cross axis, and use it to build practical one-dimensional layouts with predictable alignment and spacing.
lessons.levelTitle: Level 1: Core Web Standards & Styling Architecture

lessons.title: CSS Grid Fundamentals
lessons.description: Learn CSS Grid as a two-dimensional layout system, define rows and columns with tracks, control spacing with gaps, and place content into a predictable grid.
lessons.levelTitle: Level 1: Core Web Standards & Styling Architecture

lessons.title: Responsive Design and Media Queries
lessons.description: Learn how responsive layouts adapt to different viewport sizes using flexible sizing, media queries, and mobile-first CSS.
lessons.levelTitle: Level 1: Core Web Standards & Styling Architecture

lessons.title: CSS Challenge: Build a Responsive Interface
lessons.description: Bring the CSS module together by transforming a structured HTML page into a polished, responsive interface using the cascade, box model, typography, colors, Flexbox, Grid, and responsive design.
lessons.levelTitle: Level 1: Core Web Standards & Styling Architecture
lessons.topicTitle: Css Challenge Build A Responsive Interface

lessons.title: JavaScript and the Browser
lessons.description: Understand what JavaScript actually does in the browser, how it responds to events, and how it changes the live page through the DOM.
lessons.levelTitle: Level 1: Core Web Standards & Styling Architecture

lessons.title: Variables and Values
lessons.description: Learn how let and const give JavaScript names for values, how reassignment works, and why choosing the right declaration makes code easier to reason about.
lessons.levelTitle: Level 1: Core Web Standards & Styling Architecture

lessons.title: Data Types and Operators
lessons.description: Learn the core JavaScript data types and the operators used to calculate, compare, and combine values, with special attention to strict equality and type coercion.
lessons.levelTitle: Level 1: Core Web Standards & Styling Architecture

lessons.title: Conditions and Decisions
lessons.description: Use if, else if, else, and switch to make JavaScript choose what to do based on conditions.
lessons.levelTitle: Level 1: Core Web Standards & Styling Architecture

lessons.title: Loops and Repetition
lessons.description: Practice repeating work with for and while loops, control iteration safely, and avoid the classic off-by-one and infinite-loop mistakes.
lessons.levelTitle: Level 1: Core Web Standards & Styling Architecture

lessons.title: Functions
lessons.description: Learn how functions package reusable logic, accept inputs through parameters, and produce results through return values.
lessons.levelTitle: Level 1: Core Web Standards & Styling Architecture

lessons.title: Arrays
lessons.description: Learn how arrays store ordered collections of values and use push, map, and filter to add, transform, and select data.
lessons.levelTitle: Level 1: Core Web Standards & Styling Architecture

lessons.title: Objects
lessons.description: Learn how JavaScript objects model real-world entities with named properties, and practice reading and updating data with dot and bracket notation.
lessons.levelTitle: Level 1: Core Web Standards & Styling Architecture

lessons.title: JavaScript Mini Project
lessons.description: Build a small working learner-progress application that combines variables, conditionals, loops, functions, arrays, and objects into one coherent JavaScript program.
lessons.levelTitle: Level 1: Core Web Standards & Styling Architecture

lessons.title: Meet Your Browser DevTools
lessons.description: Get comfortable with browser DevTools and learn what the Elements, Console, Network, and Sources panels are for before using them to debug real problems.
lessons.levelTitle: Level 1: Core Web Standards & Styling Architecture

lessons.title: Inspecting HTML with Elements
lessons.description: Use the Elements panel to inspect the live DOM, experiment with HTML and CSS changes, and learn the difference between temporary browser edits and changes to your actual source code.
lessons.levelTitle: Level 1: Core Web Standards & Styling Architecture

lessons.title: Understanding the Console
lessons.description: A live message board attached to the page: what shows up there automatically, and how to tell a normal log apart from a warning or an error at a glance.
lessons.levelTitle: Level 1: Core Web Standards & Styling Architecture

lessons.title: Understanding Network Requests
lessons.description: Learn how to use the Network panel to see what a webpage requests, what comes back, whether a request succeeded, and how network evidence helps explain frontend problems.
lessons.levelTitle: Level 1: Core Web Standards & Styling Architecture

lessons.title: Your First Debugging Exercise
lessons.description: Put Elements and Console together in a guided debugging drill: inspect the page, identify evidence, explain the cause, and make the smallest fix instead of guessing.
lessons.levelTitle: Level 1: Core Web Standards & Styling Architecture

lessons.title: Understanding Browser Rendering
lessons.description: Build a clear mental model of how the browser turns HTML and CSS into the pixels you see, from parsing to layout to painting.

lessons.title: Reading JavaScript Errors
lessons.description: Learn to read JavaScript error types, messages, and stack traces so errors become useful clues instead of scary red walls of text.

lessons.title: Console Debugging
lessons.description: Use console.log, console.table, and breakpoints to inspect program state at the moment something goes wrong.

lessons.title: Debugging DOM Problems
lessons.description: Diagnose and fix common DOM failures caused by incorrect selectors, missing elements, and JavaScript running before the DOM is ready.

lessons.title: Debug Challenge: Fix the Broken Page
lessons.description: Apply DevTools, console inspection, JavaScript debugging, and DOM diagnosis together to find and fix several problems in a deliberately broken page.
lessons.topicTitle: Debug Challenge Fix The Broken Page

lessons.title: Advanced Flexbox
lessons.description: Go beyond basic Flexbox alignment by controlling wrapping, ordering, and how flex items grow, shrink, and calculate their starting sizes.

lessons.title: Advanced CSS Grid
lessons.description: Go beyond basic Grid by controlling implicit tracks, auto-placement, flexible minimum and maximum sizes with minmax(), and responsive columns with auto-fit and auto-fill.

lessons.title: Positioning and Layering
lessons.description: Practice relative, absolute, fixed, and sticky positioning together with z-index to control where elements sit and how they stack.

lessons.title: Transitions and Animations
lessons.description: Learn how CSS transitions and keyframe animations create motion, control timing and easing, and communicate state changes without turning every interaction into visual chaos.

lessons.title: CSS Architecture
lessons.description: Learn how naming conventions, file organization, and utility versus component styles keep CSS maintainable as an interface grows.

lessons.title: Design Tokens and Design Systems
lessons.description: Understand how shared design tokens centralize colors, spacing, typography, and other visual decisions so interfaces remain consistent and easier to change.

lessons.title: Advanced Responsive Design
lessons.description: Build a production-style responsive interface that combines advanced Flexbox, Grid, positioning, design tokens, and responsive constraints into one coherent system.

lessons.title: Scope and Hoisting
lessons.description: Understand where JavaScript variables are visible and why declarations behave differently depending on whether you use var, let, or const.

lessons.title: Closures
lessons.description: Understand how functions can remember variables from the scope where they were created, and use that behavior to build private state and reusable behavior.

lessons.title: The this Keyword
lessons.description: Learn why this is determined by how a regular function is called, how method calls differ from plain function calls and arrow functions, and how to avoid losing the intended this context in callbacks.

lessons.title: Destructuring and Spread
lessons.description: Practice destructuring values from arrays and objects and using spread syntax to expand or copy data concisely in modern JavaScript.

lessons.title: Array Methods
lessons.description: Use map, filter, reduce, and find to transform, select, aggregate, and locate data declaratively instead of rebuilding every operation with manual loops.

lessons.title: Modules and Imports
lessons.description: Practice using ES modules to split JavaScript into reusable files with explicit imports and exports, and learn to diagnose default-versus-named export mistakes.

lessons.title: Promises
lessons.description: Understand how Promises represent future asynchronous results, work with pending, fulfilled, and rejected states, and chain asynchronous operations with then and catch.

lessons.title: Async and Await
lessons.description: Use async functions and await to write Promise-based asynchronous code in a readable, sequential style while preserving the underlying Promise model.

lessons.title: Error Handling
lessons.description: Practice handling failures in synchronous and asynchronous JavaScript with try/catch and Promise catch, while making sure error handling provides useful recovery or user-facing feedback.

lessons.title: Modern JavaScript Challenge
lessons.description: Build a small realistic JavaScript feature that combines closures, array methods, ES modules, async/await, and deliberate error handling into one coherent application.

lessons.title: Why Version Control Exists
lessons.description: Understand why developers use version control to track change history, collaborate safely, roll back mistakes, and work on parallel changes through branches.

lessons.title: Git Fundamentals
lessons.description: Practice the core local Git workflow by initializing a repository, inspecting changes, staging files, creating meaningful commits, and reading project history.

lessons.title: Branches
lessons.description: Practice creating, switching between, and understanding Git branches so features can be developed independently before being integrated into the main line.

lessons.title: Pull Requests
lessons.description: Follow a complete pull request workflow: push a feature branch, open a pull request with a clear description, review the proposed change, respond to feedback, and prepare the branch for integration.

lessons.title: Merge Conflicts
lessons.description: Learn to read, diagnose, and resolve Git merge conflicts by understanding what both branches intended instead of blindly accepting one side.

lessons.title: Professional Git Workflow
lessons.description: Combine small focused commits, descriptive messages, feature branches, and reviewed pull requests into a repeatable Git workflow suitable for day-to-day frontend development.

lessons.title: What Is an API?
lessons.description: Understand APIs as defined contracts between software systems, and learn to read an API's endpoints, parameters, request/response shapes, and documented behavior instead of treating 'the API' as a mysterious black box.

lessons.title: HTTP Requests and Responses
lessons.description: Understand the structure of HTTP requests and responses, including methods, paths, headers, bodies, and status codes, so you can reason about network communication before using Fetch.

lessons.title: JSON
lessons.description: Understand JSON as a text format for structured data exchange and practice converting between JSON text and JavaScript values with JSON.parse and JSON.stringify.

lessons.title: HTTP Status Codes
lessons.description: Learn to read HTTP status codes as meaningful signals about the outcome of a request, with emphasis on the 2xx, 3xx, 4xx, and 5xx response classes.

lessons.title: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE
lessons.description: Understand the intended semantics of the main HTTP methods and practice choosing the appropriate method for reading, creating, replacing, partially updating, and deleting resources.

lessons.title: Loading, Error, and Empty States
lessons.description: Design and implement explicit loading, error, and empty states so data-driven interfaces remain understandable when data is delayed, unavailable, or simply absent.

lessons.title: Working with Fetch
lessons.description: Use fetch() to make HTTP requests from JavaScript, inspect the response, handle JSON data, and deliberately handle HTTP failures instead of assuming a rejected Promise means every failed HTTP status.

lessons.title: API Integration Project
lessons.description: Build a working frontend feature that consumes a real API and handles loading, success, empty, and error states without hardcoding an ideal response shape.

lessons.title: Why TypeScript?
lessons.description: Understand what problem static typing solves that plain JavaScript doesn't, and why catching errors at compile time beats catching them in production.

lessons.title: Basic Types
lessons.description: Learn TypeScript's primitive and array types, type inference, and the crucial difference between any and unknown.

lessons.title: Interfaces and Type Aliases
lessons.description: Model the shape of objects with interface and type, and know when each is the idiomatic choice.

lessons.title: Typing Functions
lessons.description: Type function parameters and return values, including optional parameters and full function type signatures.

lessons.title: Union Types and Narrowing
lessons.description: Model values that can be one of several types using unions, and safely narrow them with typeof, in, and discriminated unions.

lessons.title: Generics Fundamentals
lessons.description: Understand why generics exist — writing reusable, type-safe functions and structures — rather than treating them as unexplained syntax.

lessons.title: Typing Real-World Data
lessons.description: Type a real fetch response and API payload, extending what you learned about APIs earlier in module-2-4 with actual type safety.

lessons.title: Capstone: Convert a JS Project to TypeScript
lessons.description: Take a small existing JavaScript feature and add types incrementally, mirroring a real onboarding task on a codebase migrating to TypeScript.

lessons.title: Why React?
lessons.description: Understand the problem React solves: describing interfaces as reusable components whose rendered output changes when application state changes, instead of manually coordinating DOM updates throughout the application.

lessons.title: JSX
lessons.description: Learn JSX as the syntax React uses to describe UI, combine markup-like structure with JavaScript expressions, and practice the rules that make JSX different from ordinary HTML.

lessons.title: Components
lessons.description: Build reusable React components as focused functions that return JSX, and learn to break a growing interface into smaller pieces instead of putting everything inside one giant component.

lessons.title: Props
lessons.description: Learn how parent components pass read-only data into child components through props, and practice changing those inputs to see the child render different UI.

lessons.title: State
lessons.description: Learn how useState gives a React component local changing data, why updating state schedules a re-render, and why directly mutating state does not produce the intended React update.

lessons.title: Conditional Rendering
lessons.description: Practice choosing between JSX branches with ternaries, logical &&, and early returns so components display the correct UI for their current state.

lessons.title: Lists and Keys
lessons.description: Practice rendering arrays of data into JSX with map and learn why each rendered item needs a stable key that identifies the item across renders.

lessons.title: React Mini Project
lessons.description: Build a small React application that combines components, props, state, conditional rendering, and lists into one coherent feature.

lessons.title: Events in React
lessons.description: Wire browser events to React event handlers, pass functions correctly, and practice updating component state in response to user interactions.

lessons.title: Controlled Inputs
lessons.description: Learn how React state drives an input's value and how onChange keeps the DOM input and React state synchronized.

lessons.title: Forms and Validation
lessons.description: Build a controlled React form that validates user input, prevents invalid submission, and gives clear feedback at the right time.

lessons.title: useEffect
lessons.description: Understand when an effect is appropriate, how useEffect synchronizes a component with something outside React, and how dependency arrays determine when the effect is re-run.

lessons.title: Side Effects and Cleanup
lessons.description: Learn why effects that create subscriptions, timers, or external connections must return cleanup functions so resources are released when dependencies change or the component is removed.
